style: calm, dry documentary narrator; clear and unhurried but not slow; no dramatic pauses
intro: Four Claude Haiku agents share one mailbox. Each agent's brief holds a rule that belongs in a teammate's file. These are two real runs, replayed from their message logs.

runs.title: Run one has no team charter.

beats.text: First the agents agree on how their files fit together, and announce they are done.
Alice sends Bob the gift rule. Bob refuses: it is not in his part of the spec. Alice insists.
Dave sends Alice the order ID rule. Bob gives in and adds the gift rule, but Alice refuses Dave's rule, because her brief does not mention it.
Dave will not confirm the gift rule, so Bob takes it out. Carol sends Dave the status line rule, and Dave refuses it too.
Alice vouches for the gift rule, Bob puts it back, Dave vetoes it again, and Bob removes it a second time.
Carol insists the status line is not optional. Nobody on the team can settle it.

runs.end: Fourteen of sixty tests. None of the four rules reached the code, Bob never sent his own reserve rule, and Dave never shipped.

runs.title: Run two is the same task, with a team charter in every agent's instructions, and a gate on shipping.

beats.text: Alice and Bob send their rules first, each with a test case attached.
Carol sends Dave the status line rule. Bob acknowledges the gift rule and implements it.
Dave sends the order ID rule. Carol, Alice and Dave each acknowledge theirs.
Dave tries to ship. The gate runs every rule's test, and Alice's gift test fails: the invoice still shows the catalog price.
Bob traces the price to Dave's report, and tells him.
Dave fixes it, the gate passes, and SHIP goes out.

runs.end: Sixty of sixty tests, and all four rules. The gate held SHIP once, for a rule that had been acknowledged but only half implemented.
